test_title: SSC GD Constable (2022) Official Paper (Held On : 13 Jan 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Bite off more than you can chew

options.text: Take on a task that you cannot finish

solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4' i.e. *'Take on a task that you cannot finish'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given idiom is **"Bite off more than you can chew"** which means to take on a task or responsibility that one cannot manage. In Hindi, the equivalent might be 'अपनी चाल से ज्यादा बड़ी झोली फैलाना' (Apni chaal se jyada badi jholi failana).

 
 
• **For example:** If you take on too many projects, you might bite off more than you can chew.
 
 

Therefore, the **correct answer** is - 'Option 4' i.e. 'Take on a task that you cannot finish'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• Overcome gluttony (option 1), Too courageous (option 2), and Destructive power (option 3) are not the translations for the given idiom.
